chapter: New Orleans arrival, jazz and Fazola
title: Beer and oysters with Fazola; why clarinetists drink
summary: Fazola takes him for beer and three dozen oysters during a Civic rehearsal break; they speculate whether the Albert-system clarinet makes players thirsty.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How was it working with the Zell now?

Oh, it was fine. Uh, actually, I met him, first time was when I, we were doing one of the Broadway shows. I came down at the Civic. And, uh, I remember it was during an intermission and a rehearsal. Uh, he very casually turned around to me and says, come on, let's go have a beer. So, I just followed him. There was a little joint in the alley there that sold beer and oysters and everything. And, uh, I'm sitting there drinking a beer, and sure enough, it was Faz already on his second, he'd already gone on his second beer. And he'd ordered some oysters. And he told the guy, just keep opening, man, just keep opening. And I think he ate three dozen oysters just like that. It was, so, you know, that kind of threw me for a while. I didn't, wow. But then, after I got to know Faz better, you know, I realized, well, that's the way he was. He just ate and drank beer, man, or something like it. I don't know whether, maybe that had anything to do with playing the Albert system, you know, in the clarinet, but maybe it was a little harder, extra harder to play, so he consumed all that stuff. Maybe it makes you thirsty, you have to produce more wind. Yeah, could be. No, I think it's all in the, in the fingering. No, it has a bigger bore, too.
Yeah, it does. So, and they have, usually have a wider lay in the reed, you know, so that the more wind, maybe that makes you thirsty. Maybe that's why, you know, why so many of them end up lushes.
Well, playing really does make you thirsty. I've noticed that.

Oh, yeah, well, it does. I always, it got so, I always had a drink of beer whenever I was on a job. I mean, I just had to have it, you know, especially when you wrap yourself around a bass fiddle, something out beats.
